Text: String literals are automatically cached in the {{c1::String Pool::special heap region}}.
Extra: This avoids allocating duplicate string objects for the same character sequence.

Text: To copy or force a String reference into the String Pool, you call the {{c1::intern()}} method.
Extra: Calling this method on a dynamically created string returns its pool representation.

Text: Unlike `trim()`, the modern {{c1::strip()}} method is Unicode-aware when removing whitespace.
Extra: `strip()` is available starting from Java 11.

Text: A Text Block is opened and closed by triple double-quotes {{c1::"""}}.
Extra: The opening triple quotes must be followed immediately by a newline.

Text: `StringBuilder` is not {{c1::thread-safe::thread-safe or synchronized}} but performs faster than `StringBuffer`.
Extra: Both inherit from `AbstractStringBuilder` but `StringBuilder` is not synchronized.

Text: Starting from Java 9, the JVM uses {{c1::Compact Strings}} to optimize memory usage by encoding strings as `byte[]` arrays.
Extra: Characters that fit in Latin-1 take 1 byte; others take 2 bytes.

Text: To verify if a String is empty or contains only whitespace characters, use the method {{c1::isBlank()}}.
Extra: `isBlank()` was added in Java 11.

Text: The default initial capacity of a `StringBuilder` is {{c1::16}} characters.
Extra: This capacity is automatically expanded when more characters are appended.

Text: When a mutable character sequence grows, the new capacity is computed as {{c1::(oldCapacity * 2) + 2}}.
Extra: This prevents allocating memory too frequently.

Text: To perform literal string replacement without regular expressions, use the method {{c1::replace()}}.
Extra: `replaceAll()` parses regular expressions, which makes it slower and prone to syntax errors for literal strings.

Text: Because Strings are immutable, their hashcode is calculated once and cached in a private field named {{c1::hash}}.
Extra: This makes key-based lookups in collections extremely fast.

Text: To strip leading and trailing ASCII whitespace <= U+0020, use the method {{c1::trim()}}.
Extra: Use `strip()` for modern, Unicode-aware whitespace cleanup.

Text: In Text Blocks, the escape sequence {{c1::\s}} is used to preserve trailing whitespace.
Extra: Normally, trailing whitespace on lines inside Text Blocks is discarded by the compiler.

Text: To perform string formatting inside print streams, we use the method {{c1::System.out.printf()}} or `String.format()`.
Extra: Uses standard conversions like `%s` and `%d`.

Text: In multi-threaded environments, `StringBuffer` is safe because its mutator methods are {{c1::synchronized}}.
Extra: However, this synchronization adds lock overhead.
